newsitem.title: USA: Judge rejects mistrial motion by Simpson's lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Judge rejects mistrial motion by Simpson's lawyers.

text.p: The judge in the O.J. Simpson civil case on Monday denied a request by defence attorneys to declare a mistrial on the grounds that a dismissed juror had tainted the entire panel.

Simpson's lead attorney, Robert Baker, argued that the juror, who was removed on Friday for failing to disclose her daughter's employment in the district attorney's office, could have prejudiced other members of the panel during 2-1/2 days of deliberations.
Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki replaced Rosemary Caraway, the only black member of the jury, with an Asian-American man and ordered the panel to start deliberating from scratch.
Simpson, acquitted in October 1995 in the murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, is battling a civil wrongful-death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.

During Monday's hearing with jurors absent from the courtroom, Baker argued Caraway deliberately tried to conceal the workplace of her daughter by scratching out the words "District Attorney's Office" on her juror questionaire.
Prosecutors from the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office sought unsuccessfully to convict Simpson on murder charges stemming from the June 12, 1994, killings.
"This is a direct, deliberate attempt to mislead. I think it's an outrage," Baker angrily told the judge. "There has been jury misconduct."
Baker contended Caraway's daughter worked directly for prosecutors Christopher Darden and William Hodgman, who played major roles in Simpson's criminal trial.
"She's obviously well-connected to the prosecution," he said.

Baker demanded the remaining jurors be questioned individually to see if they were improperly influenced by Caraway and asked the judge to summon Hodgman and Darden to court to explain their relationship with her daughter.
Fujisaki refused to take any of the steps requested by the defence and told Baker he could pursue the matter further after a verdict was returned.
Plaintiffs' lead attorney, Daniel Petrocelli, successfully argued that Caraway was an "honest and conscientious" juror who made an inadvertent mistake on her questionaire.
Petrocelli also said he objected to the "defense attempt to cast some sinister aspersions on this juror," adding, "They will do anything to get a mistrial."

The judge, who rejected a similar mistrial motion from Simpson's lawyers on Friday, said he was satisfied the jury had followed his instructions to start their deliberations from scratch following Caraway's removal.
"The motion for mistrial is denied," he said.
Meanwhile, the jury of six women and six men -- made up of nine whites, one Asian-American, one Hispanic and one man of mixed black and Asian descent -- continued meeting behind closed doors.

In another development the March issue of Playboy featured a nude spread of Nicole Brown Simpson's friend, Faye Resnick, who wrote a best-selling book about the slain woman's life shortly after the killings. Simpson suggested in several interviews on television and in a book that Resnick's drug addiction was a possible motive for the murders.

In an interview with the picture spread, Resnick said she started taking cocaine only two weeks before the murders after being drug-free for two years. She also said Simpson suspected his ex-wife and Goldman were secretly dating.
"He used to see them seated next to each other at Starbucks (cafe)," she said in the interview. "He always thought they were having an affair."
"To my knowledge, they were just friends," Resnick added. "I know she thought he was quite handsome and he thought she was very beautiful, but as far as I know there was nothing but friendship."
